alternatives.name: CAPABILITY_SPLIT_PROTOCOLS_WITH_COMPOSITION_REGISTRY
tradeoffs: More interfaces to maintain than a monolithic BrokerProvider, but prevents coarse coupling and supports independent adapter replacement.

negative: Core modules must not import provider HTTP clients; import-boundary tests enforce this.
positive: Strategies and features consume canonical provider events through composition, not SDKs.

decision.summary: Provider capabilities are expressed as independently replaceable stdlib Protocol interfaces (DisclosureProvider, ReferenceDataProvider, EquityQuoteProvider, OptionChainProvider, PaperExecutionProvider) selected through a composition registry. Every provider event carries provider, entitlement, event_time, receive_time, symbol_mapping, quality, and raw_source_reference metadata.
decision.title: Capability-split provider interfaces and composition registry

effectivity.non_authorization_statement: Acceptance authorizes Phase 9 fixture-first disclosure adapter implementation only. Live broker adapters, paper execution, and non-EDGAR capabilities require separate entitlement records.
